# M5-S6: Go importers of loGo/s const views (R-U2, T-Sec6).
# Package c exports Primes (a const view over a package-level slice;
# M5-S2 const composites are not on this base), Count (a const map
# parameter), Config, and Snapshot (a const pointer result through
# rt.Freeze). A Go package in another workspace module sees plain
# []int, map[string]int, and *Config types, builds under logos, and
# runs. A Go write through the Primes result is a documented hole
# (A-GOBOUNDARY) and is not asserted here.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
mkdir $WORK/bin

cd w
logos build ./...
logos build -o $WORK/bin/interopconst$GOEXE ./g/cmd
exec $WORK/bin/interopconst$GOEXE
stdout '^primes-ok count-ok snapshot-ok$'
cd ..

-- w/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
	./l
	./g
)

-- w/l/go.mod --
module example.com/l

go 1.27

-- w/l/c/c.lgo --
package c

import "logos/rt"

var primesData = []int{2, 3, 5, 7, 11}

func Primes() const []int {
	return primesData
}

func Count(m const map[string]int, k string) int {
	return m[k] ?? 0
}

type Config struct {
	Name string
	N    int
}

func Snapshot(p *Config) const *Config {
	return rt.Freeze(p)
}

-- w/g/go.mod --
module example.com/g

go 1.27

-- w/g/q/q.go --
package q

import (
	"slices"

	"example.com/l/c"
)

var _ func() []int = c.Primes
var _ func(map[string]int, string) int = c.Count
var _ func(*c.Config) *c.Config = c.Snapshot

func Run() string {
	if !slices.Equal(c.Primes(), []int{2, 3, 5, 7, 11}) {
		return "primes-bad"
	}
	if got := c.Count(map[string]int{"a": 2}, "a"); got != 2 {
		return "count-bad"
	}
	if got := c.Count(map[string]int{"a": 2}, "missing"); got != 0 {
		return "count-missing-bad"
	}
	snap := c.Snapshot(&c.Config{Name: "s", N: 3})
	if snap.Name != "s" || snap.N != 3 {
		return "snapshot-bad"
	}
	return "primes-ok count-ok snapshot-ok"
}

-- w/g/cmd/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/g/q"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(q.Run())
}
